newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: GDP revision for 1996 underpins Singapore stocks.
newsitem.headline: GDP revision for 1996 underpins Singapore stocks.

text.p: The upward revision of Singapore's economic growth in 1996 to seven percent from a previous estimate of 6.5 percent helped to underpin the Singapore stock market on Tuesday, dealers said.
"The revision of the Gross Domestic Product to seven percent is bringing some cheer to the Singapore market," said a dealer.
On Friday, deputy prime minister Lee Hsien Loong said Singapore's economy grew by seven percent and the forecast of 5.0-7.0 percent growth in 1997 should be comfortably achieved.
At 0230 GMT, the Straits Times Industrials Index was up 5.47 points at 2,208.86.
Dealers said activity was focused on Malaysian over the counter stocks with the Malaysia bourse still closed on Tuesday for the Moslem New Year holiday.

Topping the actives were Malaysian maritime and engineering firm, Promet Bhd, and investment firm, MBF Holdings, with 9.8 million and 8.0 million shares, respectively. Of the total number of shares traded in Promet, 2.8 million were crossed at Singapore $1.405 (US$1.00), dealers said.
Singapore Press foreign led gainers, rising S$0.50 to S$28.50. Total turnover was around 73 million with gainers outpacing losers by 153 to 61.
